https://github.com/andres-erbsen/dename/.title: Clients should send writes to a leaders only
https://github.com/andres-erbsen/dename/.body: (leader = server with "IsCore = true" in config file. I should probably just rename that archaism in the conf and code) A client currently tries all servers in a loop to complete its operation (get or set). However, it is actually known ahead of time that non-leader servers are unable to handle set-s on their own, so the client should limit itself to leaders in that case. This probably requires adding a field to each server in the client config file.

https://github.com/docker/distribution/i.title: Storage driver TestStatCall modtime granularity
https://github.com/docker/distribution/i.body: Currently tests for Stat() call require modtime to be exactly to the same be with the current time. On cloud machines, that simply can't be the case and clocks can be several seconds off. if start . After ( fi . ModTime ()) { c . Errorf ( "modtime %s before file created (%v)" , fi . ModTime (), start ) } if fi . ModTime (). After ( expectedModTime ) { c . Errorf ( "modtime %s after file created (%v)" , fi . ModTime (), expectedModTime ) } Even if the time spent on the wire gets longer, the test case would simply fail: I was testing this with azure driver and encountered a failure due to one-second off, here's that: c.Errorf("modtime %s before file created (%v)", fi.ModTime(), start) ... Error: modtime 2015-01-16 20:10:02 +0000 UTC before file created (2015-01-16 12:10:03 -0800 PST) This should probably have some ɛ=±5s around the modtime value, because the point is to verify mtim works and sane. In this case even ±60s should be ok. How about: if start . Add ( time . Second * epsilon ). After ( fi . ModTime ()) { c . Errorf ( "modtime %s before file created (%v)" , fi . ModTime (), start ) } if fi . ModTime (). After ( expectedModTime . Add ( time . Second * epsilon )) { c . Errorf ( "modtime %s after file created (%v)" , fi . ModTime (), expectedModTime ) } lmk if you agree and I can send the patch. cc: @stevvooe

https://github.com/weaveworks/weave/issu.title: Unsolicited arp on new connection doesn't always work
https://github.com/weaveworks/weave/issu.body: Seen in #2313 - if we take the sleep out of the smoke-test then it usually fails the last ping. tcpdump shows that the ping is using the MAC address of the previous container, and the arp table shows this entry as REACHABLE inside the pinging container (c1). So somehow the unsolicited arp is not reaching c1 or is being ignored. Various lengths of sleep down to about 0.3 seconds let it work, but 0.2 and below make it flaky.

https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/p.title: provider/aws: Restore ah/esp protocol support for Network ACLs by catsby
https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/p.body: #8975 removed support for ah and esp string support for ingress/egress protocols in Security Groups. It seems it was too far reaching though, as while the SecurityGroup SDK/API does not support using strings for these protocols, the Network ACL API does. This PR restores support for using the string version of those protocols with Network ACLs, while still removing support for them in Security Groups. Thanks to @jrnt30 for pointing this out, and @sarkis as well in #6915 A custom TravisCI run for all TestAccAWSNet* and TestAccAWSSe* tests: https://travis-ci.org/hashicorp/terraform/builds/163436738

https://github.com/deis/registry/issues/.body: Per @bacongobbler 's request, pulling this out of #64 because it's different, yo. TL;DR: Because of moby/moby#26492 , which is symptomatic in coreos/bugs#1554 , the deis-registry throws numerous dial tcp <in-cluster ip>:9000: i/o timeout errors when trying to store docker images to minio , which may or may not surface in the deis-controller logs as either dockerclient exceptions with the same error, or gunicorn exceptions with a [CRITICAL] WORKER TIMOUT error. From what I can tell, ANY systemd-based host running docker 1.12.1 in a kubernetes cluster is at risk of suffering from this bug. It only LOOKS like an etcd issue. Top-Down (from helmc + deis -> kubernetes -> Docker + CoreOS) Because that's the road I took, and you get to come along the scenic route with me. It should be noted that while things are working fully, in many cases kubernetes appears "just fine" until you do a little digging. All of my testing where I ran into this problem was against the Alpha CoreOS channel: export KUBERNETES_PROVIDER=libvirt-coreos && export NUM_NODES=2 or 3 or 4 ./cluster/kube-up.sh # wait for etcd to settle helmc install workflow-v2.5.0 # wait for kubernetes cluster to all be ready deis pull <private registry>:5000/aergo-server:1.0.0-SNAPSHOT -a aergo-server helmc + deis Once your kubernetes cluster is up, during helmc install workflow-v2.5.0 the manifest may successfully deploy, or there could be Error from server: error when creating "STDIN": client: etcd cluster is unavailable or misconfigured. probe failed with statuscode: 503 docker + CoreOS As mentioned above, kubernetes seems to have problems maintaining a healthy connection to etcd , but those types of errors do not surface in kubernetes, as far as I could tell, except for via the cluster-info or get componentstatus commands. In other words, all pods will appear to be functioning. When you begin investigating the CoreOS VMs that host the kubernetes cluster, there are a plethora of errors - the first being the ubiquitous etcdserver: failed to send out heartbeat on time,etcdserver: server is likely overloaded ( etcd-io/etcd#5154 ), which might appear to require the addition of the heartbeat -interval and election-timeout values in the user_data.yml etcd2 section. Nope. All of this appears to belong to CoreOS coreos/bugs#1554 . However further reading brings you to moby/moby#26492 , which in conjunction with a Host OS that runs the systemd-networkd.service create a race condition that prevents the docker veth device from being associated with the in-cluster bridge network.

https://github.com/istio/old_pilot_repo/.title: Improve e2e test infrastructure
https://github.com/istio/old_pilot_repo/.body: The integration test framework has served well but we're at the limits of what it can do. Here is the call to identify any gaps in the e2e test coverage so that we can set the goals towards building a more robust test framework. Feel free to edit this issue and add more items or mark the completed items. Framework: common deploy, setup, run, log checking, teardown workflow for tests more reliable config propagation than waiting a few seconds ability to stress any feature by increasing load, repeat count test matrix to exercise feature combinations: TCP for auth, HTTP ingress for non-auth, route-splitting with auth, auth with http2 auto-upgrade, etc stabilize flaky mixer log checking due to mixer dependency, e.g. using a fake mixer full log aggregation on failures reduce log noise in debug mode ability to run subsets of tests. Useful for debug/development and if test needs to be run in parallel across multiple clusters. collect core dumps from envoy crashes make liveness probes optional to avoid crash loops Proxy: verify proxy with basic fixed configurations verify traffic redirection (i.e. iptables) regression stress tests for envoy hot restart protocol Reachability: assert two proxies on self-loops ("a" to "a") add more pods to exercise route tables for 0.0.0.0:port assert correct ports are reached grpc and http2 ports in the test app validate that NodePort and LoadBalancer services work Ingress: verify multiple paths in the ingress plaintext ingress TLS in ingress route rules applied to ingress services missing paths should return 404 Egress: HTTP single-port ExternalName service reachability HTTPS single-port ExternalName service reachability route rules applied to egress services Auth: negative test to ensure protocol is upgraded attempt to connect to a pod that doesn't belong to a service as if it belongs to a service Routing: source service based routing exact header based routing regex header based routing prefix header based routing multi-condition based routing fault injection: delay, abort weighted route rule precedence http timeout policy http retry policy Destination policies: per service version policy circuit breaking policy load balancing policy

https://github.com/gruntwork-io/terragru.title: TestNewSignalsForwarderMultiple is flaky when run from top level
https://github.com/gruntwork-io/terragru.body: Spinning this off from #194 . I was not able to cause this test to fail by running its module alone: cd shell ; go test -v -parallel 128 . However, I still see this test fail about 25% of the time when running as part of the full suite. Here's the setup: macos sierra 10.12.3 on a macbook pro. I was doing stuff on the machine during the test run (browser, shell, youtube videos) but no unusual load or anything I would expect to cause a test to fail so often terragrunt at aa9ae94 glide 0.12.3 terraform 0.9.3 Run this from top of terragrunt working copy: for i in $(seq 1 22) ; do rm -f test.out ; go test -v -parallel 128 $(glide novendor) > test.out 2>&1 ; rc=$? ; if grep "FAIL" test.out ; then echo "FAIL with return code $rc" ; else echo "PASS with return code $rc" ; fi ; done This resulted in 17 successes and 5 failures. TestNewSignalsForwarderMultiple was the only test that failed during the run. Flaky tests are difficult to debug, especially when they only flake in complex scenarios like 128 threads of simultaneous test action, so I won't be offended if you choose to close this out without a lot of action. I just wanted y'all to be aware.

https://github.com/lucas-clemente/quic-g.title: race condition when sending ConnectionClose frames
https://github.com/lucas-clemente/quic-g.body: There's a race condition when sending ConnectionClose frames, uncovered by a flaky test ( #598 ). While #599 provides a fix for the test, it doesn't solve the real problem here. The session.run() loop sends packets by calling packetPacker.packPacket() , which is the same method called to send ConnectionClose frames via packetPacker.PackConnectionClose() , which can be called concurrently by session.Close() .

https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/p.title: provider/aws: Avoid IP space overlap in EIP acc test by radeksimko
https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/p.body: This is to fix the following flaky test: === RUN TestAccAWSEIPAssociation_basic --- FAIL: TestAccAWSEIPAssociation_basic (78.86s) testing.go:280: Step 0 error: Error applying: 1 error(s) occurred: * aws_network_interface.baz: 1 error(s) occurred: * aws_network_interface.baz: Error creating ENI: InvalidIPAddress.InUse: The specified address is already in use. status code: 400, request id: 6cd28113-95fa-4080-a2c6-f3d9ede58955 FAIL The EC2 instance inside the test creates its own ENI and randomly allocates IP address for it which may happen to be the same static IP we assign to the standalone ENI. Here I'm giving it an explicit IP address to avoid the overlap.

https://github.com/concourse/concourse/i.title: Fly Execute fails with gzip: invalid magic
https://github.com/concourse/concourse/i.body: I am with the Diego development team and when we try to execute our inigo tests remotely from several machines we quite regularly (especially from my machine in Canada) get the following error when doing the upload step in the fly execute ... executing build 150754 % Total % Received % Xferd Average Speed Time Time Time Current Dload Upload Total Spent Left Speed 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 --:--:-- --:--:-- --:--:-- 0 % Total % Received % Xferd Average Speed Time Time Time Current Dload Upload Total Spent Left Speed 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 --:--:-- 0:00:59 --:--:-- 0 curl: (18) transfer closed with outstanding read data remaining gzip: invalid magic tar: Child returned status 1 tar: Error is not recoverable: exiting now exit status 2 100 42.1M 0 42.1M 0 0 303k 0 --:--:-- 0:02:22 --:--:-- 206k failed upload request failed: Put https://diego.ci.cf-app.com/api/v1/pipes/3df3e884-3b6c-40ba-6800-e04b061e2fc5: EOF The run-inigo script we use is as follows ... #!/bin/bash set -e scripts_path=./$(dirname $0) eval $($scripts_path/get_paths.sh) echo "checking code for compilation errors..." pushd $DIEGO_RELEASE_DIR/src/code.cloudfoundry.org/inigo > /dev/null for pkg in `find . -maxdepth 1 -type d ! -path . -not -path '*/\.*'`; do echo $pkg go test -c ./${pkg} > /dev/null done popd > /dev/null echo "compilation done" if [ -n "${DIEGO_CI_TARGET}" ]; then target="-t ${DIEGO_CI_TARGET}" else target="-t local" fi if [ -z "${USE_GARDEN_RUNC}" ]; then fly ${target} execute -p -x \ -c $DIEGO_RELEASE_DIR/scripts/ci/run_inigo_glinux.build.yml \ -i diego-release=$PWD \ -i garden-linux-release=$HOME/workspace/garden-linux-release \ -- "$@" else fly ${target} execute -p -x \ -c $DIEGO_RELEASE_DIR/scripts/ci/run_inigo_grunc.build.yml \ -i diego-release=$PWD \ -i garden-runc-release=$HOME/workspace/garden-runc-release \ -- "$@" fi The run_inigo_grunc.build.yml is as follows: platform: linux image: docker:///cloudfoundry/inigo-ci inputs: - name: diego-release - name: garden-runc-release params: GINKGO_PARALLEL: "true" # we check for the literal string "true" in the run_inigo script DEFAULT_EVENTUALLY_TIMEOUT: INIGO_REPEAT_COUNT: 1 SKIP_PACKAGES: SKIP_REGEX: USE_SQL: USE_GARDEN_RUNC: "true" run: path: diego-release/scripts/ci/run_inigo This does seem to occur mostly from my slower upload connection but we have also seen this happen from machines in the Pivotal SF office. Moved from vmware-archive/fly#102 /cc @andrew-edgar @vito

https://github.com/joyent/containerpilot.title: test_envvars is flaky
https://github.com/joyent/containerpilot.body: The integration test for test_envvars is racy -- we're testing that the environment variables are set via a job exec before they might be set. So occasionally we get test results like this: 2017/05/16 15:02:38 TEST: test_envvars 2017/05/16 15:02:39 control: serving at /var/run/containerpilot.socket 2017/05/16 15:02:39 PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin 2017/05/16 15:02:39 FAIL: test_envvars I believe this is a bug in the test rig rather than in the setting of the env vars themselves, but I need to look into it.

https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/p.title: Fix issue with GCP Cloud SQL Instance `disk_autoresize`  by catsby
https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/p.body: Hey @danawillow / @paddycarver ! I was looking into the following 3 failing tests as reported by our CI: TestAccGoogleSqlDatabaseInstance_basic3 TestAccGoogleSqlDatabaseInstance_maintenance TestAccGoogleSqlDatabaseInstance_slave They’re all failing with the same error message: testing.go:280: Step 0 error: Check failed: Check 2/4 error: Error settings.disk_autoresize mismatch, (true, false) I started digging in and found that indeed the value returned from the API does not match our local value in the test check here . Looking in the resource, I noticed that we only seem to save the value from the API under certain conditions here: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/v0.9.5/builtin/providers/google/resource_sql_database_instance.go#L665 if v, ok := _settings["disk_autoresize"]; ok && v != nil { if v.(bool) { _settings["disk_autoresize"] = settings.StorageAutoResize } } If I’m not mistaken, this block will only set the local disk_autoresize if that setting is found in our configuration first, and then only if that local value is true , correct? I believe this to be incorrect so I’ve patched it here. There’s also a similar issue in UPDATE where we only send a value if the new value is true , and I’ve fixed that here as well. In order to do this though, I have to add Default: false to the schema, so that we’re able to toggle from true to false (an old issue where Terraform and d.GetOk ), or otherwise settings["disk_autoresize”] may not contain a value. After fixing the read, I get the following error from the tests: TF_ACC=1 go test ./builtin/providers/google -v -run=TestAccGoogleSqlDatabaseInstance_basic3 -timeout 120m === RUN TestAccGoogleSqlDatabaseInstance_basic3 --- FAIL: TestAccGoogleSqlDatabaseInstance_basic3 (470.93s) testing.go:280: Step 0 error: After applying this step, the plan was not empty: DIFF: UPDATE: google_sql_database_instance.instance settings.0.disk_autoresize: "true" => "false" STATE: google_sql_database_instance.instance: ID = tf-lw-8275110025318672445 database_version = MYSQL_5_6 ip_address.# = 1 ip_address.0.ip_address = 35.184.210.221 ip_address.0.time_to_retire = name = tf-lw-8275110025318672445 region = us-central self_link = https://www.googleapis.com/sql/v1beta4/projects/hc-terraform-testing/instances/tf-lw-8275110025318672445 settings.# = 1 settings.0.activation_policy = settings.0.authorized_gae_applications.# = 0 settings.0.backup_configuration.# = 0 settings.0.crash_safe_replication = false settings.0.database_flags.# = 0 settings.0.disk_autoresize = true settings.0.disk_size = 0 settings.0.disk_type = settings.0.ip_configuration.# = 0 settings.0.location_preference.# = 0 settings.0.maintenance_window.# = 0 settings.0.pricing_plan = settings.0.replication_type = settings.0.tier = db-f1-micro settings.0.version = 1 FAIL exit status 1 FAIL github.com/hashicorp/terraform/builtin/providers/google 470.951s make: *** [testacc] Error 1 Which brings me to the API inconsistencies that maybe you could offer some insight into. The API docs here say that settings.storageAutoResize is default false : https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/admin-api/v1beta4/instances However, due to the way our code was written, false was never being sent... indeed it can’t be sent right now without being in ForceSendFields , because the field has omitempty on it. Even though settings.storageAutoResize is not included in the request, but future response and looking in the web console clearly shows that settings.storageAutoResize is true on the Server side. Can you poke someone on the API side about why this is ending up as true ? I see the SDK uses omitempty a lot. In order to address this, it looks like ForceSendFields is what I need here. I’ve included that as well. I’m running the tests now, and may need an additional tweak after then run to ensure everything passes, but I wanted to open this now to get your feedback on the major points. Let me know what you think!

https://github.com/ciao-project/ciao/iss.title: Remove live detatching of volumes from VM instances?
https://github.com/ciao-project/ciao/iss.body: ciao currently supports live attaching and detaching of volumes. This issue questions whether we should keep the live detaching of volumes feature. The reasons to remove it being: It only really works well on Fedora. Support on Ubuntu 16.04 is flaky. Live detaching sometimes fails and needs to be retried. This flakyiness can lead to BAT test failures as this feature is tested by BAT. Live detach doesn't work at all on Clearlinux. The QMP command we use to implement this feature is experimental. We don't have any real use case for this feature right now. It could lead to data loss if the VM is writing to the volume when it is detached by controller. The feature adds complexity to launcher and BAT which is currently hard to justify. We could remove live detach but keep live attach and detach from stopped volumes.

https://github.com/braintree-go/braintre.title: Fix flaky subscription billing day of month tests by leighmcculloch
https://github.com/braintree-go/braintre.body: What Allow subscription tests that set a billing day of month to pass if their status is active and not pending after creation. Why The tests use a fixed billing day of month of the 15th of the month. If the subscriptions are created on the 15th, the subscription will go active immediately rather than be returned in a pending state. This was causing the tests to fail on the 15th of each month.

While the first two EIPs ( nat_eip.0 , nat_eip.1 ) get allocation IDs from AWS printed out, in this example sometimes nat_eip.2 (or any other EIP) does not get a allocation ID printed out: module.vpc.aws_eip.nat_eip.1: Creation complete (ID: eipalloc-1314807a) module.vpc.aws_eip.nat_eip.2: Creation complete module.vpc.aws_eip.nat_eip.0: Creation complete (ID: eipalloc-c268fcab) There is currently exactly one code place, where the ID set to empty string explicitely: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/v0.9.9/builtin/providers/aws/resource_aws_eip.go#L137-L140 The read of EIPs happens immediately after a create, but internally the AWS control plane might need longer to propagate causing the above effect and flake. This PR makes the read of EIPs retryable. Setting the ID to empty string is not meaningful, because the resource then would not exist from a dependency graph perspective. We did not observe this flake any more with this patch. Fixes coreos/tectonic-installer#1246 @radeksimko this change is a bit more intrusive. Please advise if this is a good direction. Thanks a lot! /cc @jasminSPC

https://github.com/elastic/beats/issues/.title: Race condition on harvester limit
https://github.com/elastic/beats/issues/.body: The test_prospector.py:Test.test_harvester_limit test is flaky. The fail can be reproduced by running it in a while loop like this: while nosetests test_prospector.py:Test.test_harvester_limit; do echo .; done On my computer, this fails after 10 or 20 iterations. Looking at the logs and code , it seems to be a race condition between checking p.harvesters.Len() and p.harvesters.Start() . We could serialise the whole startHarvester() method with a new lock, but I'm slightly worried about dead locks, because the harvester registry has it's own lock. So I'm opening a ticket for now to separate this from #5449 .

https://github.com/playnet-public/gorcon.title: Fix deadlocks inside watcher and battleye subscription tests
https://github.com/playnet-public/gorcon.body: While it is still not 100% clear if those deadlocks randomly appearing when testing battleye and watcher, those definitely have to go for good. The locks are related to the subscription code responsible for adding subscribers and removing them on closed context. This is surrounded by heavy use of RWMutexes and go routines making it quite complex (maybe more complex than necessary). It would be good to revise and overthink the entire implementation, debug it or possibly rewrite it as a whole. The subscription model seems valuable and should stick with both battleye and the watcher as it is key for being that plugable in our internal API, but the problems seen here urgently need to be resolved.

https://github.com/junegunn/fzf/pull/132.title: Do not match Host config options or ?-wildcards in SSH config file by meangrape
https://github.com/junegunn/fzf/pull/132.body: Modern versions of SSH support a config option called HostKeyAlgorithms that identifies the algorithms that will be offered or accepted (in the case of SSHD). Since _fzf_complete_ssh does a case insensitive grep for host, this line--if present--is also picked up. The line being changed is: https://github.com/junegunn/fzf/blob/master/shell/completion.bash#L244 The addition is: command grep -v 'HostKeyAlgorithms |'

https://github.com/atlassian/terraform-p.title: Inter repositories resources dependencies
https://github.com/atlassian/terraform-p.body: Hello, When we are trying to create a remote, a local and a virtual repository at once the creation of the virtual repository always fails. It looks like there is no default inter resources dependencies declared yet, I don't know if we can automatically generate depends_on based on the repositories declared in a virtual repository. Another way maybe would be to retry several times to create the virtual repo waiting for the depending remote/local repositories to be created.

https://github.com/orbs-network/orbs-net.title: Acceptance TestBenchmarkConsensusLeaderGetsVotesBeforeNextBlock is flaky
https://github.com/orbs-network/orbs-net.body: This is the failure: --- FAIL: TestBenchmarkConsensusLeaderGetsVotesBeforeNextBlock (0.02s) require.go:201: Error Trace: consensus_test.go:56 network_builder.go:71 context.go:8 network_builder.go:58 consensus_test.go:42 Error: Not equal: expected: int(0) actual : uint64(0x11) Test: TestBenchmarkConsensusLeaderGetsVotesBeforeNextBlock Messages: initial getBalance result on leader This is the line it fails on: committedTamper := network.GossipTransport().Fail(adapter.BenchmarkConsensusMessage(consensus.BENCHMARK_CONSENSUS_COMMITTED)) committedLatch := network.GossipTransport().LatchOn(adapter.BenchmarkConsensusMessage(consensus.BENCHMARK_CONSENSUS_COMMITTED)) network.SendTransferInBackground(0, 0) // send a transaction so that network advances to block 1. the tamper prevents COMMITTED messages from reaching leader, so it doesn't move to block 3 committedLatch.Wait() // wait for validator to try acknowledge that it reached block 1 (and fail) txHash := network.SendTransferInBackground(0, 17) // this should be included in block 2 which will not be closed until leader knows network is at block 2 committedLatch.Wait() FAILS ----> require.EqualValues(t, 0, <-network.CallGetBalance(0), "initial getBalance result on leader") This failure is strange because due to the Tamper failing, the block should not be committed, so getBalance on the leader should not return 17

https://github.com/spacemeshos/go-spacem.body: Overview / Motivation Our CI tests and even local tests fail from time to time without any real error from our logic. gRPC is only minimally implemented and yet fails frequently. this makes our tests flaky. The Task find the root of the problem and solve. it seems like its easy to reproduce the test failing in travis-CI or other linux environments. though it also happens on macs from time to time. the error we get is : all SubConns are in TransientFailure also a more long description of the issue is mentioned in the comment below. Implementation Notes the tests we run are under api/api_test.go Time Estimate 4 hours Contribution Guidelines Introduce yourself on go-spacemesh dev chat channel - ask our team any question you may have about this task Fork branch develop to your own repo and work in your repo You must document all methods, enums and types with godoc comments You must write go unit tests for all types and methods when submitting a component, and integration tests if you submit a feature When ready for code review, submit a PR from your repo back to branch develop

https://github.com/ethersphere/swarm/pul.title: Fix data races in TestLDBStoreCollectGarbage by janos
https://github.com/ethersphere/swarm/pul.body: This PR addresses race condition described in #1118 and a similar one in gc tests. This change solves data races, but it does not solve failing tests when go test tool is called with -race. Tests are failing with not all expected chunks deleted by the garbage collection. If tests are run without the -race flag, they are passing as usual. Currently, the flaky test is disabled. We agreed on the standup not to dedicate more time to this failing tests, as regular tests are passing and we are working on a different gc implementation.

https://github.com/bblfsh/javascript-dri.title: Two identical parse requests can return different results
https://github.com/bblfsh/javascript-dri.body: Guys, I found one really weird big in bblfsh. I think it is related to daemon itself but cannot be 100% sure. So do not hesitate to move this issue if I am wrong. Context Machine learning team really want to have reproducible results everywhere where it is possible. So we fix all random seeds to have a deterministic code. Suddenly we find out that two identical runs of style-analyzer quality estimation give different results: src-d/style-analyzer#557 . Clues lead to bblfsh and I was able to reproduce the bug without our code. Let me show you. How to reproduce Run in bash docker run -d --rm --name style_analyzer_bblfshd --privileged -p 9432 \: 9432 \ bblfsh/bblfshd \: v2.11.0 --log-level DEBUG docker exec style_analyzer_bblfshd bblfshctl driver install \ javascript docker://bblfsh/javascript-driver \: v2.6.0 # clone repo with data git clone https://github.com/laravel/telescope git checkout 6f0a10ec586cfa1a22218b6778bf9c1572b97912 Also checked for v1.2.0 driver version. Run in python3 from collections import defaultdict import pickle import time import os import bblfsh bc = bblfsh . BblfshClient ( "localhost:9432" ) res = defaultdict ( lambda : defaultdict ( int )) times = defaultdict ( list ) iter_n = 10 for i in range ( iter_n ): for ( dirpath , dirnames , filenames ) in os . walk ( "telescope" ): for filename in filenames : try : t_start = time . time () filepath = os . path . join ( dirpath , filename ) if ".git" in filepath : continue resp = bc . parse ( filename = filepath ) if len ( res [ filepath ]) > 0 and resp . status not in res [ filepath ]: print ( "iter %.3d New status %d for filepath %s. counter: %s " % ( i + 1 , resp . status , filepath , dict ( res [ filepath ]))) res [ filepath ][ resp . status ] += 1 times [ filepath ]. append ( time . time () - t_start ) except Exception as e : print ( filepath , e ) res [ filepath ][ repr ( e )] += 1 I do not think it is important but bblfsh package version is 2.12.6 . My output head telescope/resources/.DS_Store Content must be UTF-8, ASCII or Base64 encoded telescope/resources/.DS_Store Content must be UTF-8, ASCII or Base64 encoded iter 003 New status 2 for filepath telescope/webpack.mix.js. counter: {0: 2} telescope/resources/.DS_Store Content must be UTF-8, ASCII or Base64 encoded telescope/resources/.DS_Store Content must be UTF-8, ASCII or Base64 encoded iter 004 New status 2 for filepath telescope/resources/js/routes.js. counter: {0: 3} iter 004 New status 2 for filepath telescope/resources/js/base.js. counter: {0: 3} How to interpret Mainly, if you see the message, that some file gets a new status that means that during the identical requests bblfsh return different statuses. For example, for telescope/webpack.mix.js and telescope/resources/js/routes.js it was able to parse file first but not the second time. Notes If you set iter_n to bigger number you get much more output messages. Sometimes performance for big iter_n become super bad. Can be related to perf: bblfshd 2.9 non responsive after parsing 1000+ files bblfshd#226 If you feed only js files it works great and always parse them for iter_n=100 . So it is important for ML team to have reproducible output from bblfsh. Please tell me if you are able to reproduce the issue or need more info from my side.

https://github.com/virtual-kubelet/virtu.title: use shared informers and workqueue by pires
https://github.com/virtual-kubelet/virtu.body: This PR reworks how VK implements its Kubernetes controller: Replaces the current manual mechanism of event watching and processing with using: two shared informer factories (one for Pod , and one for ConfigMap and Secret ), and a work queue. The pod shared informer factory is constrained via WithTweakListOpts so that it only produces events for pods that have been assigned to the current node. The work queue bits were mostly drawn from from https://github.com/kubernetes/sample-controller , with a minor adjustment so we can stop processing a pod after its reconciliation has failed N times. ResourceManager is no longer needed as informers' listers can be used to read Kubernetes resources, but since the ResourceManager is used in the ACI provider test, I decided not to remove it at this point. We can think about it as we progress. Closes #405

https://github.com/loomnetwork/loomchain.title: Make e2e test runner retry commands that fail while a cluster is starting up
https://github.com/loomnetwork/loomchain.body: We've got some flaky e2e tests (like coin) that fail every so often due to what I suspect is a timing issue. My theory is that the QueryServer starts up before the TM node has properly initialized and queries attempt to access app state before the TM node has called Application.BeginBlock and loaded the app state. So we may need to fix QueryServer to return some kind of "not ready" error from endpoints that require access to the app state. Then the e2e test runner should auto-retry any command that errors out with "not ready".

https://github.com/elastic/beats/pull/10.title: Ensure kubernetes caches don't expire if they are being read by jsoriano
https://github.com/elastic/beats/pull/10.body: Some metrics in metricbeat kubernetes module are cached during a time, if they are not updated they are removed. But it is usual to have pods or containers that are not updated during more time that the expiration cache. Current implementation was not renovating expiration times for cache entries so all were eventually removed if updates for them are not received. Replace it with the cache implementation available in libbeat, but keeping the existing interface. Also, use slashes instead of dashes to generate unique container uids. Dashes can be used by kubernetes names, what could lead to ambiguous keys for the caches. Fix #10658

https://github.com/rook/rook/pull/2991.title: ceph mds: update keyring before deployment update by BlaineEXE
https://github.com/rook/rook/pull/2991.body: Because the deployment update-and-wait function waits for the deployment to be ready, and that cannot happen due to the keyring not having been updated yet. The keyring has its owner set to the deployment so that no special keyring handling must be done, but it must be created after the deployment UID is known. Change the order of operations so that the existing deployment's UID can be retrieved if it exists and the keyring created/updated before the update-and-wait function is called. This order-of-operations issue currently only applies to the mds. Other daemons whose keyrings are owned by the replication controller do not use the update-and-wait function. https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/5789.title: Skip waiting for paused deployments by perher
https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/5789.body: What this PR does / why we need it : In my chart I have multiple Deployments for different micro-services in my application. Some of the services have upgrade dependencies or requires special logic to perform rolling upgrade. To facilitate this I set those deployments to be in paused state before the chart is upgraded. When running helm upgrade with paused deployments and when using the --wait flag, the upgrade processed is stalled forever (or until timeout) since Kubernetes will not perform rolling upgrade on paused deployments. I propose to have Tiller ignore paused deployments altogether when waiting for a upgrade to finish since these will otherwise block the upgrade process.

https://github.com/kata-containers/runti.title: shim v2: Close vhostfd after vm get vhostfd by xs3c
https://github.com/kata-containers/runti.body: If kata containers is using vfio and vhost net，the unbinding of vfio would be hang. In the scenario, vhost net kernel thread takes a reference to the qemu's mm, and the reference also includes the mmap regions on the vfio device file. so vhost kernel thread would be not released when qemu is killed as the vhost file descriptor still is opened by shim v2 process, and the vfio device is not released because there's still a reference to the mmap. Fixes : #1669 Signed-off-by: Yang, Wei [REDACTED_EMAIL]

https://github.com/sensu/sensu-go/issues.title: Proxy check requests are scheduled too infrequently
https://github.com/sensu/sensu-go/issues.body: It appears that events for proxy check requests are not updated each interval. Rather, the splayed executions are not scheduled until after the whole interval. Expected Behavior 60 second check interval, 2 proxy entities, 50% splay: 60s between proxy1 executions 60s between proxy2 executions 15s between proxy1 -> proxy2 execution Current Behavior 60 second check interval, 2 proxy entities, 50% splay: 90s between proxy1 executions 90s between proxy2 executions 15s between proxy1 -> proxy2 execution Possible Solution Splayed executions should be scheduled immediately, not after the original interval. Steps to Reproduce (for bugs) Create the following proxy entities { "type": "Entity", "api_version": "core/v2", "metadata": { "name": "proxy1", "namespace": "default" }, "spec": { "deregister": false, "deregistration": {}, "entity_class": "proxy", "last_seen": 0, "subscriptions": null, "system": { "network": { "interfaces": null } } } } { "type": "Entity", "api_version": "core/v2", "metadata": { "name": "proxy2", "namespace": "default" }, "spec": { "deregister": false, "deregistration": {}, "entity_class": "proxy", "last_seen": 0, "subscriptions": null, "system": { "network": { "interfaces": null } } } } Create the following check { "type": "CheckConfig", "api_version": "core/v2", "metadata": { "name": "check-proxy", "namespace": "default" }, "spec": { "check_hooks": null, "command": "echo hi", "env_vars": null, "handlers": [], "high_flap_threshold": 0, "interval": 60, "low_flap_threshold": 0, "output_metric_format": "", "output_metric_handlers": null, "proxy_entity_name": "", "proxy_requests": { "entity_attributes": [ "entity.entity_class == 'proxy'" ], "splay": true, "splay_coverage": 50 }, "publish": true, "round_robin": false, "runtime_assets": null, "stdin": false, "subdue": null, "subscriptions": [ "proxy" ], "timeout": 0, "ttl": 0 } } Start the backend Start the agent ( --subscriptions proxy ) Executions are 90 seconds apart: sensuctl event info proxy1 check-proxy --format json | jq .check.history Executions are 90 seconds apart: sensuctl event info proxy2 check-proxy --format json | jq .check.history Context With the check splay and proxy entity configurations, each check should execute every 60 seconds (and 15 seconds apart from each other: 60 second interval * 50% / 2 entities = 15 second splay). The current behavior is not at parity with 1.x or docs. Reported by AdamskiEM / @adammcdonagh in the community slack. Your Environment Sensu version used (sensuctl, sensu-backend, and/or sensu-agent): 5.9.0 Installation method (packages, binaries, docker etc.): binaries Operating System and version (e.g. Ubuntu 14.04): MacOS

https://github.com/loadimpact/k6/issues/.title: metrics show incorrect timings
https://github.com/loadimpact/k6/issues/.body: Response.timings.receiving show unbelievably low values, like 0.05 (ms). In my tests, when receiving content of 2-3 MB, duration is typically 700ms and waiting time is (almost) the same with 1 ms accuracy, sending and receiving taking together about 0.1 ms. Tested with k6 v0.24.0. I can't believe the numbers and I have double-checked my code (and also timings.duration = timings.sending + timings.waiting + timings.receiving), so I'm quite sure there must be a bug in k6 metrics code.

https://github.com/dedis/cothority/issue.title: Tests only work with leader
https://github.com/dedis/cothority/issue.body: While working on #2001 , some tests showed up that only work if the leader is contacted. This seems bad in most cases, and should be extended to also work for non-leaders. As far as I can tell, often something like this happens: AddTransaction is sent to a node, it returns as soon as this node processed the transaction GetProof is sent to two nodes, the node who doesn't have the transaction is faster and returns an empty proof All tests that use byzcoin.Client.UseNode are suspicious: byzcoin.TestClient_GetProof byzcoin.TestClient_GetProofCorrupted byzcoin.TestSecureDarc byzcoin.TestService_SetConfigRosterReplace byzcoin.TestService_SetConfigRosterReplace byzcoin.Client.DownloadState byzcoin.contracts.TestDeferred_ScenarioMultiInstructions_ byzcoin.contracts.TestDeferred_ScenarioMultipleSigners byzcoin.contracts.TestDeferred_ScenarioUpdateConfig byzcoin.contracts.TestDeferred_SimpleDelete byzcoin.contracts.TestDeferred_PublicDelete byzcoin.contracts.TestInsecureDarc calypso.TestService_ReshareLTS_Different calypso.TestClient_CreateLTS calypso.TestClient_Calypso calypso.TestService_ReshareLTS_OneMore eventlog.Client personhood.Tests The following is good: byzcoin.simulation.SimulationService.Run , because all transactions need to be sent to the same node, else the counters are not correct TestContract_Write_Benchmark - same reason: multiple transactions with same signer

https://github.com/atlassian/gostatsd/is.title: TestDispatchMetricsShouldDistributeMetrics is flaky
https://github.com/atlassian/gostatsd/is.body: --- FAIL: TestDispatchMetricsShouldDistributeMetrics (0.01s) handler_backend_test.go:148: Error Trace: handler_backend_test.go:148 Error: Not equal: expected: 304 actual : 303 Test: TestDispatchMetricsShouldDistributeMetrics handler_backend_test.go:153: aggregator 0 was invoked 63 time(s) handler_backend_test.go:153: aggregator 1 was invoked 62 time(s) handler_backend_test.go:153: aggregator 2 was invoked 59 time(s) handler_backend_test.go:153: aggregator 3 was invoked 56 time(s) handler_backend_test.go:153: aggregator 4 was invoked 63 time(s) Seems to fail 1-2% of the time. Race related: wg.Wait() // Wait for all metrics to be dispatched cancelFunc() // After all metrics have been dispatched, we signal dispatcher to shut down wgFinish.Wait() // Wait for dispatcher to shutdown We dispatch all the metrics then cancel the backend as soon as they're in the pipeline. The backend handler may not have drained the pipeline before we cancel it. Oddly TestDispatchMetricMapShouldDistributeMetrics doesn't seem to have the same failure. It does a DispatchMetricMap on the same goroutine but there's still channels to process it. It's not immediately obvious what the difference is (it might just be much rarer)

https://github.com/govim/govim/issues/40.title: ci: fix flaky tests in signs & quickfix_config test cases
https://github.com/govim/govim/issues/40.body: What version/commit of govim are you using? Latest master, 54b65c8 What did you do? I've noticed that test scripts that involves calls to vim's sign_getplaced(...) is flaky. The reason is that PublishDiagnostics callback is sometimes used to determine when the signs are updated, e.g. from cmd/govim/testdata/signs.txt : # Fixing the last quickfix entry should remove the last sign vim call append '[5, "\tvar v string"]' [vim] [!vim:v8.1.1711] vim ex 'doautocmd TextChangedI' # make sure gopls is notified if incremental buffer updates isn't supported errlogmatch -wait 30s 'PublishDiagnostics callback: &protocol.PublishDiagnosticsParams{\n\S+:\s+URI:\s+"file://'$WORK/main.go vim -indent expr 'sign_getplaced(\"main.go\", {\"group\": \"*\"})' ! stderr .+ cmp stdout placed_nosign.golden Since PublishDiagnostics callback is parsed to quickfix entries and then signs, there is a time window where the quickfix and signs aren't updated yet. If sign_getplaced(...) is called too quickly, it might return the signs that is about to be removed. Those tests must rely on something other than PublishDiagnostics callback that happens after quickfix is done updating.

https://github.com/elastic/beats/pull/12.title: Fix keyspace configuration in redis key metricset by jsoriano
https://github.com/elastic/beats/pull/12.body: Fix incoherent behaviour when keyspace is specified in the redis host URL and not in some of the key patterns. If it was not specified it used the default 0 instead of using the one in the redis host. Redis doesn't have a direct way to request the keyspace being currently used by a client, documentation mentions that is responsibility of the client to keep track of the keyspace used if it changes it using Select . This solution stores the db number originally configured and uses it in the key metricset if no other keyspace is configured. Fixes #12874

https://github.com/orbs-network/orbs-net.body: Describe the bug test assumes that once a block has been written, all subsequent write attempts will be of the same height, namely, the next expected height. But in reality, background sync operations can flakily try to sync previously written blocks. normally we tolerate these race conditions and ignore them as long as a fork is not detected. but this test ignores this possibility and fails when they happen Steps To Reproduce reproduced upon merging reputation (non related) PR into master. assumed to be flaky Logs https://circleci.com/gh/orbs-network/orbs-network-go/18690?utm_campaign=workflow-failed&utm_medium=email&utm_source=notification <autogenerated>:1: Error Trace: lean_helix_recovers_from_disk_error_test.go:45 network_harness.go:171 panic.go:19 panic.go:13 network_harness.go:156 concurrency.go:37 network_harness.go:153 network_harness.go:134 Error: Not equal: expected: 0x3 actual : 0x4 Test: TestLeanHelix_RecoversFromDiskError/CONSENSUS_ALGO_TYPE_LEAN_HELIX Messages: expected the same height to be attempted after write failure

https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/.title: Firefox menus activate but are invisible in full screen mode
https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/.body: Reported by Palacee_hun on 2011-06-28 16:35 To reproduce this: In any FF 3.6 document window switch to fullscreen mode by hitting F11 or from View menu. This works immediately. If you have no sight, you can check whether fullscreen mode is on by querying the status bar (NVDA+End) or by trying to invoke menus by Alt+letter combinations (e.g. Alt+f goes to file menu). In fullscreen mode neither succeeds, while in normal mode both does obviously. Try to go back to normal mode by pressing F11. Then perform the check described above. You will find that FF is still in fullscreen mode. It seems you can repeat pressing F11 as many times as you like, FF won't switch back to normal mode. Unload NVDA while still in the FF document window. Now press F11. Relaunch NVDA, then check for fullscreen mode. Alas, you'll find that normal mode returned as it should! This step proves that this issue has got something to do with NVDA, not just with FF. FF 4 and 5 and IE may exhibit the same behaviour with NVDA, I couldn't test them. This issue seems to be reproducible Both with NVDA 2011.1.1 and 2011.2 beta1. It doesn't seem to matter which version you use in the FF 3.6 series, all seem to work the same in this aspect. This issue has significance because some irregular or badly programmed web content can only be interacted with object navigation and/or mouse routing (NVDA+/) and they sometimes can only be clicked on when in fullscreen mode (otherwise mouse pointer wouldn't be routed to them correctly). However in fullscreen mode you can't use the menu shortcuts and other FF keyboard shortcuts and you can't query the status bar, so you'd want to switch back to normal mode as soon as fullscreen mode is not needed.

https://github.com/SoftwareIntrospection.title: Git rename and copy detection flaky
https://github.com/SoftwareIntrospection.body:
The Issue Git itself doesn't track renames or file copies. Even when using git mv it internally still added the content of that file to the new filename and removed the old file. Having set that, it's possible to tell git to try to find copies or file moves. For this it uses heuristics, which hunks of which files are identical. If a file is moved without changed contend, git tells 'R100' (R for rename), which mean that the stated files have 100% content in common. Since this is a heuristic this can go wrong. See the following example: user@user:~/repos $ mkdir git_log_bug user@user:~/repos $ cd git_log_bug user@user:~/repos/git_log_bug $ git init Initialized empty Git repository in /Users/user/repos/git_log_bug/.git/ user@user:~/repos/git_log_bug (master) $ echo "Hello World
Hello Universe" >> first_file.txt user@user:~/repos/git_log_bug (master) $ echo "Hello World
Hello Universe" >> second_file.txt user@user:~/repos/git_log_bug (master) $ git add first_file.txt second_file.txt user@user:~/repos/git_log_bug (master) $ git commit -m "initial commit" [master (root-commit) b996586] initial commit 2 files changed, 2 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-) create mode 100644 first_file.txt create mode 100644 second_file.txt user@user:~/repos/git_log_bug (master) $ git rm first_file.txt rm 'first_file.txt' user@user:~/repos/git_log_bug (master) $ echo "Hello some more" >> second_file.txt user@user:~/repos/git_log_bug (master) $ git mv second_file.txt renamed_second_file.txt user@user:~/repos/git_log_bug (master) $ git add renamed_second_file.txt user@user:~/repos/git_log_bug (master) $ git commit -m "second commit" [master f11add4] second commit 2 files changed, 1 insertions(+), 1 deletions(-) rename first_file.txt => renamed_second_file.txt (63%) delete mode 100644 second_file.txt So far so good. Runing a git log --name-status without copy or rename detection yields the following (simplified): user@user:~/repos/git_log_bug (master) $ git log --name-status commit f11add4431f7cd8e93218ea2c222df1063dc8da1 Author: Alex <[REDACTED_EMAIL]> Date: Mon Sep 12 17:25:00 2011 +0200 second commit D first_file.txt A renamed_second_file.txt D second_file.txt Now with rename and copy detection it states this (simplified): user@user:~/repos/git_log_bug (master) $ git log --name-status -C -M commit f11add4431f7cd8e93218ea2c222df1063dc8da1 Author: Alex <[REDACTED_EMAIL]> Date: Mon Sep 12 17:25:00 2011 +0200 second commit R063 first_file.txt renamed_second_file.txt D second_file.txt user@user:~/repos/git_log_bug (master) $ git show -C -M f11add4431f7cd8e93218ea2c222df1063dc8da1 commit f11add4431f7cd8e93218ea2c222df1063dc8da1 Author: Alex <[REDACTED_EMAIL]> Date: Mon Sep 12 17:25:00 2011 +0200 second commit diff --git a/first_file.txt b/renamed_second_file.txt similarity index 63% rename from first_file.txt rename to renamed_second_file.txt index 7894def..194ec9c 100644 --- a/first_file.txt +++ b/renamed_second_file.txt @@ -1 +1,2 @@ Hello World
Hello Universe +Hello some more diff --git a/second_file.txt b/second_file.txt deleted file mode 100644 index 7894def..0000000 --- a/second_file.txt +++ /dev/null @@ -1 +0,0 @@ So all in all, it detects the wrong file renamed! Now this could be ok, if it's consistend. The situation BUT this is not consistend: CVSAnalY itself uses the flages -M and -C for rename and copy detection. The extension CommitLOC only uses -M (aka --find-renames , in my tests -C didn't made a difference) and Patches are also generated using --find-renames ( PatchLOC , Hunks and indirectly HunkBlame uses those patches). Since they don't always match this sometimes yield to File id for some-renamed.file @ 1234 not found The solution? One thing could be to enable copy detection on Patch creation to patch CVSAnalY and all the results of the patch creation. Whit this hunks of copied files essentially would be empty. But with this the file id should always be findable. @lewisham and @linzhp : What do you think? PS: this is related to https://github.com/SoftwareIntrospectionLab/repositoryhandler/

https://github.com/h5py/h5py/issues/3.title: Flaky behavior on 32-bit platforms where dimensions > 2**32 are involved
https://github.com/h5py/h5py/issues/3.body: Original author: [REDACTED_EMAIL] (October 07, 2008 23:26:47) A few places in the codebase don't like dimensions bigger than a long int. The official policy, on both 32 and 64 bit platforms, is: h5py must accept large (64-bit) dimensions anywhere HDF5 does The maximum dimension size allowed is the limit of a signed 64-bit int (roughly 2**63). The following steps will address this issue: Identify every API call which can take a dimension > 2**32 and add unit test conditions which explicitly check large values Since len cannot return a value larger than 2**32 in 32-bit Python, add a custom len() method to each class which can requires this behavior. Add a description of this policy to the documentation Original issue: http://code.google.com/p/h5py/issues/detail?id=3

https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy.title: ken wants FK attributes to load on pending with an option for transient too
https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy.body: Migrated issue, originally created by Michael Bayer ( @zzzeek ) the attached patch begins to address this. many more tests will be needed. Highlights include: the mechanism by which we determine if we should use "committed" attributes or not changes. This part of the patch I like regardless. Persistent objects do a better job of loading related objects with this behavior and the approach is simple - only use the "committed" state if we're in a flush. attribute events send through a flag that still disables loading on pending to get a transient to load, just set its session_id. this is fairly clean and sneaky enough not to confuse new users. backrefs need to be more careful about things I've worked with this all day, and I still don't think load-on-pending is a great idea most of the time, it issues more autoflushes, more useless SELECT statements, more complex logic needed to guess if the SELECT is wasteful - and the load on transient thing is entirely special case stuff. That aspect of the functionality is pushed into a relationship() flag load_on_pending . Attachments: load_on_fks.patch

https://github.com/elastic/beats/pull/13.title: Check if file has disappeared sooner in Log reader by ycombinator
https://github.com/elastic/beats/pull/13.body: Resolves #13889 . This PR teach the Log reader to check file stat related changes, e.g. a file being moved or renamed, more aggressively than before. As a result a slow or flaky output can no longer hold up these checks from being performed.

https://github.com/saltstack/salt/issues.title: The orchestrate runner falsely reports "States ran successfully." (likely due to missing reply or timeout from minion).
https://github.com/saltstack/salt/issues.body: The following steps was reproduced on Fedora 20 but can be similarly done on any other OS. Setup Create a simple state file which installs any uninstalled package (here: bind ): # path: /srv/salt/deleteme.sls install_dns_server: pkg.installed: - name: bind Use this state in orchestration : # path: /srv/salt/deleteme_orchestration.sls install_dns_server_with_orchestration: salt.state: - tgt: 'minion_id' - sls: deleteme Now make sure that yum somehow fails to install any package. For example, you may set wrong DNS in /etc/resolv.conf or add a non-existing proxy to /etc/yum.conf like here: # Proxy settings proxy=http://whatever:8000/ proxy_username=whatever proxy_password=whatever Try running yum install bind manually to confirm it fails. Problem Run orchestrate runner: salt-run -l debug state.orchestrate deleteme_orchestration > results.yaml The debug output does not produce any [ERROR ] . Check results: # results.yaml control: ---------- ID: install_dns_server_with_orchestration Function: salt.state Result: True Comment: States ran successfully. Changes: Summary ------------ Succeeded: 1 Failed: 0 ------------ Total: 1 This is clearly _false _ because: rpm -qi bind package bind is not installed Moreover, running the initial state using salt-call fails perfectly: salt-call -l debug state.sls deleteme > results.yaml ... [INFO ] Executing command 'repoquery --queryformat="%{NAME}_|-%{VERSION}_|-%{RELEASE}_|-%{ARCH}_|-%{REPOID}" --all --pkgnarrow=installed' in directory '/root' [ERROR ] The following packages failed to install/update: bind. ... Check results: # results.yaml local: ---------- ID: install_dns_server Function: pkg.installed Name: bind Result: False Comment: The following packages failed to install/update: bind. Changes: Summary ------------ Succeeded: 0 Failed: 1 ------------ Total: 1 Versions Both master and minion are deployed on the same Fedora 20 x86_64 host. salt --versions-report Salt: 2014.1.4 Python: 2.7.5 (default, Feb 19 2014, 13:47:28) Jinja2: 2.7.1 M2Crypto: 0.21.1 msgpack-python: 0.1.13 msgpack-pure: Not Installed pycrypto: 2.6.1 PyYAML: 3.10 PyZMQ: 13.0.2 ZMQ: 3.2.4

https://github.com/ros/ros_comm/issues/4.title: rosmaster doesn't close sockets properly, hangs
https://github.com/ros/ros_comm/issues/4.body: Steps to reproduce: Start roscore Launch rosout repeatedly: while :; do rosrun rosout rosout; done Monitor CLOSE_WAIT sockets: lsof | grep rosmaster | grep -c CLOSE_WAIT The number of sockets keeps steadily climbing until the open file limit is hit. rosmaster then becomes unresponsive (e.g. rostopic list or rosnode list both just hang) and starts consuming 100% CPU. Versions: Ubuntu 12.04.5 LTS ros-hydro-desktop-full 1.0.2-0precise-20140807-2038-+0000 Background: While starting rosout in a loop isn't the most sensible thing, it's just the minimal test case to reproduce this. Trying "rosnode list" or "rostopic list" doesn't leak sockets in the same way. I've had a few instances of this happening and it probably hasn't been rosout (but due to other pressures I haven't had the time to figure out the flaky component)

https://github.com/pyfarm/pyfarm-master/.title: Add search capabilities necessary for the agent to either create or update its own definition by opalmer
https://github.com/pyfarm/pyfarm-master/.body: This change includes a couple of new feature, bugfixes, and some api improvements. The goal here was the give the agent the ability to search for itself more easily without requiring as many GET requests. A full list of changes are below and this change also makes the progress towards fixing pyfarm/pyfarm-agent#16 . Add url arguments to /api/v1/agents/ for hostname , port , and ip . This was needed so the agent can search for itself using a GET request before deciding what to do. Changed POST /api/v1/agents/ to always create a new agent instead of create or merge since GET on this endpoint now allows us to find the specific agent we can post updates to at /api/v1/agents/<id> Includes the above url arguments in the resulting output. This was also required so that if there are multiple entries for the same hostname there's enough unique information to make sense of it on the agent without another GET request. Changed the output for a search to return None and NOT_FOUND if no hosts matching the query are discovered. Split out most of the url parameter tests for /api/v1/agents into individual tests Added assert_contents_equal to the base test class. This is used to make sure that two iterables contain the same data without caring about order. This was done instead of using sort each time since we don't particularly care about order. Added the get_request_argument utility function. This is similiar to request.args.get except it can produce an error message if we get an unexpected type in a url argument. Moved from datetime.now -> datetime.utcnow in the mixin responsible for setting time_finished and time_started . The tests for this were passing on travis but were flaky on my local host, this change fixes that flakiness without breaking the tests on travis. Modified empty responses to return null instead of a dictionary. For most responses, especially NO_CONTENT , this is the better thing to do since an empty dictionary is technically not an empty document.

https://github.com/pyfarm/pyfarm-agent/p.body: This change is centered around improving coverage of some of our existing code base as well as fixing bugs found in the process. In addition to this the change also: Ensures trial --until-failure tests does not terminate due to flaky tests. Provides HTML/API views with some standardized tests for things such as implemented methods, schemas, etc, Removes a couple HTML views which have been sitting around unimplemented for a while. These are things we will implement later but don't have anything but stand-in code at the moment. Adds some new coverage exclusions for system dependent tests or areas which are not internal to the agent or its execution. Most notable are the command line tools and the logger, both of which are covered by other tests as they are used. This change does not expand on coverage for service.py or the new http.api.update module because these are areas that are still undergoing direct development.

https://github.com/ioos/compliance-check.title: CF check rejects many valid units
https://github.com/ioos/compliance-check.body: Running the CF tests on some IMOS files, we get high-priority tests failing with messages like these: units are metres, standard_name units should be m units are Celsius, standard_name units should be K The CF convention says "The value of the units attribute is a string that can be recognized by UNIDATA's Udunits package" ( Section 3.1 ) and "Unless it is dimensionless, a variable with a standard_name attribute must have units which are physically equivalent (not necessarily identical) to the canonical units " ( Section 3.3 ). Looking at the code (cf.py), the function check_units seems to insist on the units being exactly the canonical units for any variable with a standard_name attribute, but makes some exceptions to allow some commonly used variants. These exceptions include e.g. "meter" and "meters" (US spelling), but not "metres" (British/Australian spelling). Wouldn't it be more correct (and more flexible) to check the units using the tests of equivalence provided by UDUNITS? (e.g. udunitspy.udunits2.Unit has a method are_convertible )

https://github.com/box/ClusterRunner/iss.title: If a slave fails to post results back to master, there's no retry or error logic to handle it, slave hangs indefinitely
https://github.com/box/ClusterRunner/iss.body: I'm running into a situation while running tests where we will see sporadic failures after a slave finished executing a subjob and calls Network.post to send the results back to master. If the POST call fails, the slave does not check the return code and will wait for new jobs to be assigned indefinitely. This causes the build to hang because the master hasn't received results back for all the subjobs. I'm trying to add some additional logging to some of the slave classes and/or retry logic on the post call, but I'm not too familiar with the code. I've attached some of the logs from the slave below, let me know if you see something. [2015-02-19 11:06:18.634] DEBUG Bld63-Sub15 project_type Command completed with exit code 0. [2015-02-19 11:06:25.852] WARNING Bld63-Sub15 decorators Call to Network.post raised ConnectionError("HTTPConnectionPool(host='ip-10-110-90-25.us-west-2.compute.internal', port=43000): Max retries exceeded with url: /v1/build/63/subjob/15/result (Caused by <class 'ConnectionResetError'>: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer)"). Retrying in 0.1 seconds. [2015-02-19 11:06:25.970] INFO Bld63-Sub15 cluster_slave Build 63, Subjob 15 completed and sent results to master.

https://github.com/ibis-project/ibis/iss.title: ImpalaTemporaryTable ignores impyla's threadsafety level which corrupts cursor state
https://github.com/ibis-project/ibis/iss.body: This also causes test suite flakiness. Sometimes, the GC is called in the midst of impyla's _execute_sync , which goes on to use the same cursor for ImpalaTemporaryTable 's DROP TABLE command. This corrupts the state of the cursor during the query execution.

https://github.com/pantsbuild/pants/issu.title: Python Thrift caching issue with included Thrift files
https://github.com/pantsbuild/pants/issu.body: Test case available on the thrift-include branch of https://github.com/wyattanderson/pantstest/tree/thrift-include Problem Under-invalidation when modifying transitive Thrift dependencies of a Thrift target. We have a Thrift API in A.thrift that imports B.thrift and C.thrift . B and C are consumable via separate targets as well. A depends on B and C in the BUILD file in addition to importing them: python_thrift_library( name='A', sources=[ 'A.thrift', ], dependencies=[ ':B', ':C', ] ) python_thrift_library( name='B', sources=[ 'B.thrift', ] ) python_thrift_library( name='C', sources=[ 'C.thrift', ] ) The most reliable reproducer I can find is in a project with artifact caching enabled, make a change to C.thrift and run/build a Python target that depends on A.thrift . The changes won't be picked up unless you clean-all . Setup Clone the repository ./pants binary src/python:test && dist/test.pex Expected output: ['C', 'read', 'thrift_spec', 'validate', 'write'] Uncomment lines 5-7 in src/thrift/C.thrift ./pants binary src/python:test && dist/test.pex Expected output ['C', 'Cba', 'Cfoo', 'Cfoobar', 'read', 'thrift_spec', 'validate', 'write'] Actual output ['C', 'read', 'thrift_spec', 'validate', 'write'] If you run ./pants clean-all , you get the expected output, which makes me think this is an artifact caching issue. The actual problem we're seeing in production is even stranger: the addition of a new type to the equivalent of the C.thrift file doesn't get included in the built PEX.

https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/P.title: Fio: pre-filling the attached disk does not work
https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/P.body: Look at the fio_benchmark.Prepare() method: fill_size = str(DISK_USABLE_SPACE_FRACTION * 1000 * disk.disk_size) + 'M' Let's say that disk.disk_size is 3 and DISK_USABLE_SPACE_FRACTION is 0.9. fill_size will be exactly 2700.0M . This format is not accepted by fio and as a result, pre-filling the scratch volume will not work. What is worse, fio command will fail with exit_code=0 and we will not even see that something went wrong. My proposition would be: convert fill_size to int before converting it to str (format like 2700M is accepted by fio) add more logging around fio command as it sometimes exits without error code.

https://github.com/jeffwidman/bitbucket-.title: Issues can be created out of order
https://github.com/jeffwidman/bitbucket-.body: I'm currently attempting to migrate https://bitbucket.org/jaraco/hgtools . I'm using the jaraco/bitbucket-issue-migration#refactor-and-python3 to get the keyring support, but the technique for importing the issues into github should be the same. When I run the migration, I get different results for different runs. In a recent test, I ran: python migrate.py jaraco hgtools jaraco jaraco/hgtoolstest Which yielded lines including: Created bitbucket issue 27 (27/31): hgtools is a weird name [1 comments] ... Created bitbucket issue 31 (31/31): Automatic versioning breaks if mercurial repository is synced with a GIT upstream through hg-git extension [0 comments] Created 31 issues However, despite the script having created the issues in order, that issue 27 appears as issue 28 . Looks like issue 31 was processed as 25 . But the behavior is not deterministic. In another run, there were more and different discrepancies. It seems there may be a race condition in the Github issue importer such that it can get some issues out of order. I'm not yet sure what can or should be done.

The numbers in model_class5-test_parameters5 where the crash appears vary, I also already had a successfull compilation of astropy 1.1 All build logs for MIPS are here . The crashes only appear on the big endian machines; for little endian everything for version 1.1+ is fine . It is, however, probably not an endianness problem; other big-endian architectures (like s390) compile without problems . It is not unlikely that this is a problem of our build machines (I already experienced some flakiness there); so the bug report is more for completeness -- and if others observe similar.

https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/P.title: background_cpu_test.py is flaky
https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/P.body: I've hit this twice so far in the automated tests that run for each pull request. Example failure: ====================================================================== FAIL: Check that the background_cpu_threads flags overrides the config ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Traceback (most recent call last): File "/home/travis/build/GoogleCloudPlatform/PerfKitBenchmarker/tests/background_cpu_test.py", line 129, in testBackgroundWorkloadVanillaConfigFlag self._CheckVMFromSpec(spec, 2) File "/home/travis/build/GoogleCloudPlatform/PerfKitBenchmarker/tests/background_cpu_test.py", line 81, in _CheckVMFromSpec expected_remote_post_stop) AssertionError: 3 != 4 '3 != 4' = '%s != %s' % (safe_repr(3), safe_repr(4)) '3 != 4' = self._formatMessage('3 != 4', '3 != 4') >> raise self.failureException('3 != 4') background_cpu_test patches out commands like vm.Install or vm.RemoteCommand, then calls BenchmarkSpec.Prepare, which is expected to call those VM functions, and finally checks how many times the patched functions were called. The problem is that the BenchmarkSpec commands call the patched functions in a different thread per VM: PerfKitBenchmarker/perfkitbenchmarker/benchmark_spec.py Line 233 in c5e2c39 vm_util . RunParallelThreads ( targets , len ( targets )) The default MagicMocks used to patch the functions do not appear to be threadsafe. Example: import sys import threading import mock _CALLS_PER_THREAD = 100 _THREAD_COUNT = 1000 _EXPECTED_CALL_COUNT = _CALLS_PER_THREAD * _THREAD_COUNT def Hello(): pass def CallHello(): for _ in range(_CALLS_PER_THREAD): Hello() module = sys.modules[__name__] with mock.patch.object(module, 'Hello'): threads = [] for _ in range(_THREAD_COUNT): t = threading.Thread(target=CallHello) threads.append(t) for t in threads: t.start() for t in threads: t.join() print 'call_count is {0} (expected {1})'.format( module.Hello.call_count, _EXPECTED_CALL_COUNT) I suspect background_network_workload_test.py may also be vulnerable as well, but I haven't encountered a failure on it yet.

https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/.title: Update GCE module to use JSON credentials by viglesiasce
https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/.body: This fixes issue #13515 in a backwards compatible way. GCP now recommends using JSON credentials files rather than P12 files. Using JSON files also simplifies the onboarding process for Ansible as it no longer requires openssl-foo in order to get started. This PR updates includes the following: Bumps the required libcloud version to 0.17.0 which allows for JSON credentials Adds a parameter credentials_file that supplants pem_file Adds documentation for configuring via environment variables Adds documentation for using GCE service accounts rather than JSON files Updates the examples to use the new credentials_file parameter This PR has a counterpart in the ansible-modules-core repository that enables this functionality in the modules themselves. That one should be merged first or at the same time. cc @erjohnso

https://github.com/blaze/datashape/issue.title: promote(string, ?string) still returns ?object
https://github.com/blaze/datashape/issue.body: Hello, After updating to datashape==0.5.2, I had hoped that #213 would fix my issue, but it didn't. I'd like > >> promote ( dshape ( "string" ), dshape ( "{a: ?string}" ). subshape [ 'a' ]) to return Option(ty=ctype("string")) but it actually returns Option(ty=ctype("object")) . The special casing added by that PR doesn't get hit because dshape("string") != ctype("string") : > >> dshape ( '{a: string}' ). subshape [ 'a' ] ctype ( "string" ) > >> dshape ( 'string' ) dshape ( "string" ) > >> dshape ( '{a: string}' ). subshape [ 'a' ] == dshape ( 'string' ) False i.e. a Mono leaf node in the datashape tree does not compare equal to a DataShape node wrapping that leaf node. Ideally, I'd like to be able to compare the lhs and rhs here as equal. In talking with @llllllllll , we saw a couple options: Change DataShape.__eq__ to compare only shape and measure instead of type. Remove the box when the tree is only a box around the Mono, possibly by short circuiting DataShape.__new__ and returning the single Mono parameter. This looks to require updating blaze as well, since there are checks for whether a DataShape is being passed around, and this change would mean dshape("string") would NOT return a DataShape instance. Do you agree with the intent here? What's the right path?

https://github.com/saltstack/salt/issues.title: [PY3] Top File Merge order is variable instead of lexicographical
https://github.com/saltstack/salt/issues.body: Description of Issue/Question The order that top files are merged in by default has changed when running Salt with Python 3. We have a couple of tests to check for this - the expected way that top files will be merged/ordered by default is lexicographically when running Salt in Python 2. Python 3 seems to treat lists more as traditional lists - they are unordered and results will vary. I tried to track this down, but the solution isn't immediately apparent to me. I think the problem has something to do with our DefaultOrderedDict class and the way it is instantiated in the get_tops function where we instantiate the default_factory as a list , but I am just guessing. That might be a red herring. Either way, this will affect the expected ordering of top files and environments and will be a regression for people when they switch to Python 3. Setup I found this issue when running the highstateconf unit tests with Python 3. Steps to Reproduce Issue Set up the test suite to run with Python 3 and run: python3 tests/runtests.py -n unit.highstateconf_test There will be two test failures: test_basic_merge and test_ordered_merge . These fail because the order of the top files in the merge_tops and get_tops function calls is now variable and unordered. In Python 2, these lists were always ordered lexicographically, and the assertEqual would pass. Versions Report Develop branch: # salt --versions Salt Version: Salt: 2016.3.0-1055-g0329f57 Dependency Versions: cffi: 0.8.6 cherrypy: 5.0.1 dateutil: 2.4.2 gitdb: 0.6.4 gitpython: 1.0.1 ioflo: 1.5.5 Jinja2: 2.8 libgit2: Not Installed libnacl: Not Installed M2Crypto: 0.21.1 Mako: Not Installed msgpack-pure: Not Installed msgpack-python: 0.4.6 mysql-python: 1.2.3 pycparser: 2.10 pycrypto: 2.6.1 pygit2: Not Installed Python: 2.7.6 (default, Jun 22 2015, 17:58:13) python-gnupg: 0.3.8 PyYAML: 3.10 PyZMQ: 14.5.0 RAET: Not Installed smmap: 0.9.0 timelib: 0.2.4 Tornado: 4.2.1 ZMQ: 4.0.5 System Versions: dist: Ubuntu 14.04 trusty machine: x86_64 release: 4.5.5-x86_64-linode69 system: Linux version: Ubuntu 14.04 trusty ping @cachedout @thatch45 and @meggiebot

https://github.com/gtagency/buzzmobile/i.title: Investigate test flakyness
https://github.com/gtagency/buzzmobile/i.body: When writing ROStests, it is necessary to spin up roscore and ros nodes and have them communicate. This requires multiple system threads to run in sync. https://github.com/ethereum/web3.py/issu.title: Strange error from `ethereum.tester`
https://github.com/ethereum/web3.py/issu.body: What was wrong? On most commands this comes out of standard out when the interpreter exits. Exception ignored in : < bound method state . __del__ of < ethereum . tester . state object at 0x11350ca20 >> Traceback ( most recent call last ): File "/Users/piper/python-environments/web3.py/lib/python3.5/site-packages/ethereum/tester.py" , line 187 , in __del__ AttributeError : 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'rmtree' What is going on? This is a race condition that occurs when the interpreter is shutting down. The upstream library eth-testrpc needs to be patched so that it doesn't create the instance of the tester client on module import but rather on demand somehow.

https://github.com/snapcore/snapcraft/pu.title: elf: cleaner patchelf experience by sergiusens
https://github.com/snapcore/snapcraft/pu.body: Use the patchelf on the system by default if not running from the snap and if it fails instruct the user to use patchelf as a part or as a build-snaps entry. Given that when using as a part the user can choose to not use filters to remove the file from prime, we also make a copy of the file to patch (breaking any potential existing hard link with the other steps) to avoid the problem of trying to patch the patchelf primed file with the same patchelf binary file. https://github.com/mesonbuild/meson/pull.body: This test covers usage of generated files in static_library that is later linked into shared_library. This test is flaky because dependencies are not set correctly. Tests are not robust because the only way I found to trigger this reliably is building with -j20 . But it randomly fails at least in specific test case so it might be good enough. 5th test is what actually fails, all the rest is just a verification that something very similar works fine. I copied build.ninja below, the difference between 4th and 5th tests is that I replaced link_with with link_whole , and dependency on header file disappeared. Since header file is created by generator and dependency does not exist, ninja will not necessary execute generator before trying to compile main.c.o , and this will manifest in missing meson_test_function.h . Note that -j20 is helpful because it forces ninja to execute everything at the same time. https://github.com/cylc/cylc-flow/issues.title: newly flaky test hold-release/13-ready-restart.t
https://github.com/cylc/cylc-flow/issues.body: This test overrides the job submit command to sleep 10 for task foo-1 and then does a quick shutdown --now --now to stop the server after foo-1 is submitted and is in the "ready" state (due to the sleep). Then on restart --hold the ready task should reload to held and run after release with the job submit command restored. As of recently(the change to the process pool maybe?) foo-1 sometimes, but not always, goes to "submit-failed" immediately after the shutdown command (but well before the sleep ends). This breaks the test because the task then restarts as "submit-failed" instead of ready.

https://github.com/stevenleeg/geemusic/i.title: Music not playing
https://github.com/stevenleeg/geemusic/i.body: I've been trying to get the skill to work and it's driving me a bit mad. I've got it set up using the UK English instructions, I am starting using foreman, in a virtual environment, and using ngrok. Everything works as expected. The skill responds saying "Playing album x by y" or whatever is relevant, it appears to have found a streaming link, but the music just won't play. I have checked the .env values several times, I don't have the trailing '/' or '/alexa'. I've checked through the instructions carefully multiple times and everything appear to be correct. The only things I could see that could perhaps be a problem are the server is running on port 5000 rather than 4000, but I've had a look around some of the other issues posted and that doesn't seem to be unusual. Also I am getting a 400 after every request. e.g. 07:53:12 web.1 | 127.0.0.1 - - [16/Feb/2017 07:53:12] "GET /stream/Thcn3dx45gqvphgmb2j65umeo3i HTTP/1.1" 302 - 07:53:13 web.1 | 127.0.0.1 - - [16/Feb/2017 07:53:13] "POST /alexa HTTP/1.1" 400 - I'm running Arch Linux on a raspberry pi 3, everything is up to date. Any help would be appreciated. :) Cheers. edit: interestingly I just noticed even though no music is playing I can ask "what is currently playing" and get the response consistent with the track/album/artist I was looking for.
